newsitem.title: USA: Coast Guard delays opening section of Mississippi.
newsitem.headline: Coast Guard delays opening section of Mississippi.

text.p: The U.S. Coast Guard said it delayed reopening of a key deep-draft shipping lane at the mouth of the Mississippi River while it surveys depths in the swollen channel.

A survey boat is making passes through the Southwest Pass at the mouth of the Mississippi to make sure shipping will be safe through the channel, the only entrance to the river from the Gulf of Mexico for deep-draft freighters and tankers, Coast Guard Cmdr. Ken Parris said.
The U.S. Army Corps of Engineers also has four dredging boats working to clear the pass of mud lumps and sand bars that can form in the swirling currents of the rising river.
The Norwegian-flagged freighter Ariel, bound for the United Kingdom with a load of coal, grounded overnight on a mud lump near the mouth of river.
After the freighter was refloated, local pilots had expected shipping through the river's Southwest Pass to resume today with restrictions on ships with over 40-foot drafts.
